schema_note: Curated list of ALL deviations from the 2000-km threshold clustering (see docs/decisions/003-graph-schema.md, Point 1). Two categories: force_same_landmass (clusters are merged despite being > 2000km apart, because they sit on the same landmass) and accepted_separate (multiple hubs are deliberately accepted, because they are genuinely separate landmasses). Every country whose raw clustering yields more than one cluster MUST appear in exactly one of the two lists -- otherwise the build fails (see build_landmass_groups() in scripts/build_graph.py). This is the safeguard against 'country X splits apart in the future, but nobody noticed'.

force_same_landmass.note: The mainland incl. Alaska/west coast + east coast is one contiguous landmass; the 2000-km threshold only splits them because of sparse cable coverage in between. Hawaii stays deliberately separate (real ocean in between).
West coast/British Columbia + Atlantic provinces are one contiguous landmass.
East coast + northwest are one contiguous landmass.

accepted_separate.note: After the force_same_landmass merge above, Hawaii remains a second, deliberately separate hub -- real ocean, not a landmass split.
Tarawa + Tabwakea/Kiritimati -- genuinely separate landmasses, opposite sides of the 180th meridian.
